newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to open telecoms market wider.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to open telecoms market wider.

text.p: Singapore moved to open its telecommunications market further on Wednesday, announcing it would call for tenders later this year for one or two more licences to run local mobile phone services from 2000.

Minister for Communications Mah Bow Tan told reporters this meant up to four companies could operate domestic mobile telephone services from 2000 and encouraged foreign companies to bid for the licences.

"There is a need for us to expand the cellular telephone market," Mah said. "There is a case to have up to four licences but we reserve the right to have only one more. Four will be the maximum for the foreseeable future."
Singapore's mobile telephone market is currently a monopoly operated by state-owned Singapore Telecommunications Ltd but a second operator, MobileOne, will enter the market in April.

MobileOne is a consortium comprising Keppel Corp and Singapore Press Holdings, each holding 35 percent stakes, with Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications each holding 15 percent.

"The Telecommunications Authority of Singapore (TAS) will be calling for tenders later this year to award up to two more cellular licences for provision of services from April 2000," Mah announced in a speech to a business group.
The number of licences awarded would depend on the quality and attractiveness of the offers, he said. Foreign companies could own up to 49 percent of any bidding consortium.

Mah said the consortiums preparing to tender for Singapore public basic telecommunication services (PBTS) licences from 2000, which will allow companies to operate land-based telephone networks, were also invited to bid for the cellular licences.

"The time schedule of the cellular service tender has been synchronised with the PBTS main tender exercise," to allow successful bidders to start basic and mobile telephone services at the same time, he said.
Results of the mobile tenders would be announced in mid-1998, giving the winners 18 months to get their networks ready.
Singapore has said it will award one or two new licences for basic telephone services.
TAS said in a statement the licences for mobile services would be valid for 17 years from April 1, 2000 to coordinate their expiry with the length of the licence given to MobileOne.
Analysts said Mah's announcement had been expected and predicted heavy competition for the licences.
"I think there will be keen bidding for the licences," said David Toh, technologies analyst at ING-Barings.
"Many of the companies looking at the basic telecoms licences will consider bidding for the cellular licences," he added.
Analysts said the state-owned Singapore Technologies group was likely to be in the running for a new licence. It had bid unsuccessfully for the licence won by MobileOne.
Another contender might be diversified local maritime group SembCorp, which had recently signalled its interest to bid for a basic telecoms licence, they said.
